title: Do SAE Features Transfer Across Fine-Tuning? A Systematic Probe

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: if SAE features do not transfer across fine-tuning, all SAE-based safety monitors trained on base models give false assurance on deployed models. Directly relevant to the interpretability-to-safety bridge.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: SAELens provides pre-trained SAEs, and Gemma-2-2B variants are publicly available. Measuring cosine similarity and probe accuracy is standard. Requires some SAE background but tools are accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused: take pre-trained SAE on base model, run inference on fine-tuned variants, compute feature overlap metrics. Clear metrics (cosine similarity, reconstruction quality, probe accuracy). Achievable in 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: The core question has been directly answered by UniReps (2025) and EMNLP (2025) papers studying SAE feature transfer across base and fine-tuned models.

evidence.source: UniReps Blog (2025) - Do SAEs transfer across base and finetuned LMs?
evidence.finding: Directly studies SAE transferability from base to fine-tuned models on Gemma-2b and Mistral-7B. Finds significant degradation for Gemma-2b but reasonable transferability for Mistral-7B.

evidence.source: SAE Features for Classifications and Transferability (EMNLP 2025)
evidence.finding: Introduces methodology for evaluating SAE-based features in classification tasks including cross-model transfer from Gemma 2 2B to 9B-IT, achieving macro F1 > 0.8.

evidence.source: Training Superior SAEs for Instruct Models (2025)
evidence.finding: Addresses the gap between base model SAEs and instruction-tuned models by training SAEs specifically for instruct models.

evidence.source: LessWrong - SAE transfer across base and finetuned models
evidence.finding: Community analysis showing residual activation similarity is highly correlated with SAE transferability, with model-dependent results.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: This exact question has been directly studied and published. The UniReps blog post (2025) specifically investigates SAE transferability across base and fine-tuned language models using the same models proposed (Gemma-2b, Mistral-7B). The EMNLP 2025 paper demonstrates cross-model SAE feature transfer. A separate paper addresses training SAEs specifically for instruct models. The core research question is largely addressed, though systematic probing across more model families and fine-tuning types could add incremental value.
